STOCKER game review Self Test

Pressing the self-test switch on the chassis tray will cause the program to enter a sequenced self-test mode. First the screen RAM is tested by outputting a pattern to the mon- Itor and checking it. This part of the test takes about 10 seconds and results tn status screen that Indicates whether the screen RAM Is good and also indicates the status of the ROM checksums, Pressing start will then go to the switch Input test where the state of al] the controls and option switches are presented to the user. Pressing start again will take the user to the game score statistics screen where a cumulative graph of scores and other Information {s presented to the viewer, Pressing start again will take the user to a simijiar game time statistics screen. On either this screen or the prior one, the user may choose to reset the cumulative statistics and high scores by pressing the gearshift lever twice. Pressing start yet again returns the user to the switch Input screen, To exit selftest mode, the self-test switch must be returned to Its original position on the game chassis.
Attract Mode

1, When game is first powered on or when self-test mode is exited, a blank screen with the message "one moment please" appears for approximately 30 seconds. (This is to allow the sound circuitry to be initiallzed)
2. Title screen will appear (approx. 10 seconds)
3. High score screen will appear (approx. 10 seconds) 4, Demonstration screen will appear (approx, 10 seconds) 5, Credits screen will appear (approx. 10 seconds)
6. Cycle repeats from Step 2.
Game Nescription

Stocker 1s a one player top-down driving game. The object of the game Is to drive from Florida across the southern United States to California. The player is represented by a bright orange stock car and Is controlled by a steering whee! and a hi/low gear shifter. The player's game time Is determined by the "fuel" In the player's gas tank as represented by the fuel gauge on the right side of the screen. A player has a number of opportunities in the game to replenish part of that fuel supply by pulling into gas stations situated along the route, A player "refuels" by running across the flashing red gas square in the service station, A player's score Is determined by a combination of factors that include

1) maintaining a high average speed, 2) crossing state IInes whIch are good for a 5000 point bonus and 3) getting as few tickets as possible. A player gets a ticket if he has broken the law (denoted by chasing cop cars and sirens) and he is tagged or touched by a pursuing cop car. If a player can make it across a state line before a cop tickets him he is free from pursuit until! he breaks the law again. A player breaks the law by elther running cross-country off the roadway or by hitting a non=pursulng cop car. Note that one game option causes the game to end when a player has received three tickets but normally the game ends when a player runs out of fuel. It is also possible to "win" the game by making It across the finish tine in California. Any player doing so receives an extra game completion bonus of 5000 polnts and extra points for any remaining fuel he has left. Note that alternate routes are also available to the player at particular points In the game. These are designated by a question mark and the player Is left to determine the most optimum route through the game. Other pertinent Information presented to the player Is given on the "instrument" panel at the right side of the game. This Includes a digital speedometer, ticket Indicator, message read-out area for state IIne bonuses or tickets, and a miniature map of the current state the player Is In. Score Is given along the top of the screen and is continually updated during game play.
